title: 01. product-artifacts substrate -- docs/product/ family, slug script, and artifact-family.md

labels.name: pre-planning
labels.description: Product lifecycle work upstream of /deep-plan

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

The suite is flat with no orchestrator, so the whole composition burden falls on whatever the beats chain through. This builds it: `docs/product/<slug>/` as a folder family sibling to `docs/plans/<slug>/`, plus the script that resolves slugs into it, creates folders, answers whether one exists, and reports drift. Nothing else in the suite can start until a beat has somewhere to write.

One part is new work rather than a port. Every spec-driven system surveyed uses the same folder-of-named-members shape -- spec-kit, Kiro, BMAD -- and none of them detects that a downstream document went stale after its upstream changed. So the provenance line and freshness check have nothing to copy, and their semantics have to be pinned by a test here.

## Blocked by

None. Everything else in the batch waits on this.

## Deliverables

- **`skills/product-artifacts/scripts/product_artifact.py`**, standard library only, four entry points:
  - `--resolve-slug` -- normalise and collision-check against `docs/product/`, reporting the slug, whether it collides, and the auto-incremented suffix that would resolve it. For writers.
  - `--ensure-folder` -- create the folder and refresh its row in the `docs/product/` index, following the generated-region convention `docs/plans/README.md` already uses.
  - `--check-freshness` -- report which members are stale. Addressable at a single slug, not only across the family.
  - `--exists` -- return the normalised slug and whether the folder is present. **For readers.** Issue 10 (#24) is the family's first, and without this it would have to read `--resolve-slug`'s collision flag as an existence hit. That works, and it silently breaks the day someone adjusts collision semantics for the writer, because the coupling is invisible from the writer's side.
- **`skills/product-artifacts/references/artifact-family.md`** -- the single home for three facts the beats cite rather than restate: each member's required H2 sections, the provenance format `**Derived from**: <upstream member> (<git blob sha>)`, and the staleness rule.
- **A change to `skills/deep-plan/scripts/resolve_slug.py`** generalising it to two families. The normalisation rules must keep existing exactly once in the repository. Draw the seam deliberately: normalisation, collision detection and the suffix are shared, while the legacy flat-file collision check and the `## Context` extraction are plans-family knowledge. `docs/product/` has neither, so those come in as arguments rather than becoming the default for both.
- **`skills/product-artifacts/tests/`** pinning the closed member set, the provenance format, and each behaviour under Constraints.

The member set is closed at five, in chain order: `brief.md`, `discovery.md`, `requirements.md`, `spec.md`, `roadmap.md`. Each but the first opens with the provenance line.

**The staleness rule.** Its permanent home is `artifact-family.md`; it is restated here only so this issue stands alone, and that file wins on any disagreement. The sha is `git hash-object` over the upstream's content at the moment the member was written -- a pure function of content, needing no commit. A member is stale when that command over its upstream today returns a different sha. This says nothing about whether the change mattered: detecting movement is mechanical and cheap, judging whether the downstream needs rewriting is a human call.

## Constraints

- **Staleness is a finding, not an error.** `--check-freshness` exits 0 on stale members and on unresolvable ones (missing upstream, absent or malformed provenance line), and says which of the three states it found per member. Its only non-zero path is its own inability to run.
- **`--ensure-folder` is idempotent**, and the folder and the index row are one operation -- creating one without the other has ensured nothing.
- **Standard library only**, and the tests run with no git repository present, which is why blob-hash semantics are specified rather than shelling out to `git`.
- **State the cross-skill reach explicitly.** Nothing in the repository does one today, and the only precedent is a same-directory sibling import that does not generalise. It must work from a working directory other than the repository root.
- **`docs/plans/` is unchanged**: `test_resolve_slug.py` passes, the slug rules live in one module, `docs/plans/README.md` is byte-identical. Refactors are fine -- extracting `finalize_plan.py`'s `regenerate_index` so both families call it is in scope if the plans index comes out identical. A second hand-written copy of the marker convention is not.
- Inherits the epic's constraints.

## Out of scope

Every authoring skill in the suite. All template content -- `artifact-family.md` fixes each member's H2 *names*, not what goes under them. Any change to `docs/plans/` content, its index, or its member set. The bridge (issue 10 (#24)). Deciding what to do about a stale member. An invocable `SKILL.md`: this is a shared script and reference package the beats call, not a ninth skill competing for the description budget -- if one proves unavoidable, say why in the pull request rather than adding it silently.

## References

- The four decisions this inherits, and the twelve cross-cutting constraints: the epic, #14.
- Generalise or imitate: `skills/deep-plan/scripts/resolve_slug.py`, `finalize_plan.py` (`regenerate_index`), `docs/plans/README.md`.
- The reader that needs `--exists`: issue 10 (#24).
- Prior art: https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/spec-driven.md · https://kiro.dev/docs/specs/ · https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md
- The drift gap this fills: https://www.augmentcode.com/guides/living-specs-for-ai-agent-development

title: 02. product-brief skill -- turn a raw idea into a customer-facing PR-FAQ

labels.name: pre-planning
labels.description: Product lifecycle work upstream of /deep-plan

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

First beat. Turns a raw product idea into a customer-facing narrative *before* any solution is designed. Writes `docs/product/<slug>/brief.md`, the head of the chain, which every later beat reads.

The template is Amazon's PR-FAQ, written as if the product had already launched. It forces the author to state the customer, the problem and the value in plain language with nowhere for an implementation to hide -- the discipline missing when work starts at `/deep-plan`. One structural feature must survive: the two FAQ sections are *separate*, external customer-and-press and internal leadership, and merging them is the documented most common corruption of the format.

One risk is specific to a *generated* PR-FAQ and has no precedent to copy. The internal FAQ demands market sizing, projections and competitive landscape; the press release demands customer quotes. A model asked for that document will produce plausible numbers and quotes whether or not anyone knows them, and an invented TAM is worse than a blank one because it gets cited downstream as input. So the skill must distinguish what the user supplied from what it does not know, and mark the second rather than filling it.

## Blocked by

Issue 01 (#15). The only write target is `brief.md`, reached through `--ensure-folder`.

## Deliverables

- **`SKILL.md`** -- reads its template and principles file at run time rather than restating them, and names `product-discovery` as its successor. A flat suite has no orchestrator, so sequencing exists only where a skill body states it.
- **`references/pr-faq-template.md`** -- three structurally separate parts:
  1. A one-page mock press release: heading, subheading, a summary paragraph with outlet and date, a problem paragraph naming the target market rather than gesturing at "users", solution paragraphs stating what differentiates this from what exists, and a close with quotes and a how-to-get-started.
  2. An external FAQ: pricing, how it works, support, availability.
  3. An internal FAQ: competitive landscape, market sizing, technical/legal/operational risks, and an explicit what-has-to-be-true assumption list.

  This file also defines the suite's **unknown marker**: one literal token, used in every slot that would otherwise carry an unsourced figure. Issues 03 (#17) through 07 (#21) reuse it and none may define a second.
- **`references/product-brief-principles.md`** -- four clusters, each a documented PR-FAQ failure mode: **solution-first writing** (built from what the team can build rather than from a customer problem); **selling rather than truth-seeking** (written to get approved rather than to surface why the idea might fail); **discounting existing workarounds** ("no alternative exists today", without naming what customers do right now); **solving a non-meaningful problem** (real, but not worth anyone's money or attention).
- **`tests/test_product_brief_contract.py`.**

Lean Canvas and the Business Model Canvas appear in the principles file as cited comparison points and nowhere else -- named so a reader sees what was not chosen, and because their classic failure (filling Solution before validating Problem) is the same as cluster 1. Not alternate templates, not reachable by flag.

## Constraints

- **Never invent a fact.** Sizing, projections or competitive detail the user did not supply carry the unknown marker naming what is missing and who would know it. Press-release quotes are permitted as the format's aspirational device but are visibly marked as authored-for-the-brief, not collected evidence.
- **The two FAQs stay distinct sections.** Three parts existing is the floor; the FAQs being separate is the point.
- **`brief.md` carries no provenance line** -- it heads the chain. The substrate's test pins that; the two tests must not contradict each other.
- Inherits the epic's constraints. Note this issue *defines* the unknown marker (constraint 9) rather than reusing it.

## Out of scope

Every other beat. Any change to the substrate -- if its interface looks wrong, open a follow-up against issue 01 (#15). Reviewing a written brief (issue 08 (#22)): this ships the rubric, not the critic. Validating the brief's claims -- ranking assertions and designing tests for them is `product-discovery`, and the what-has-to-be-true list is an input to that beat, not a completed analysis. Any change to `docs/plans/`, `/deep-plan`, or the existing four skills. A framework menu, a `--template` flag, or a canvas output mode.

## References

- The four decisions this inherits, and the twelve cross-cutting constraints: the epic, #14.
- Imitate: `skills/design-review/SKILL.md` + `references/design-principles.md`, `skills/tdd-review/tests/`.
- PR-FAQ structure and its anti-patterns: https://workingbackwards.com/resources/working-backwards-pr-faq/
- Cited comparison points only: https://www.strategyzer.com/library/the-business-model-canvas · https://leanstack.com/lean-canvas

title: 03. product-discovery skill -- turn a brief's claims into ranked, testable assumptions

labels.name: pre-planning
labels.description: Product lifecycle work upstream of /deep-plan

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

Second beat. Reads `brief.md`, writes `discovery.md`: the claims a brief rests on, turned into ranked testable assumptions.

It exists because a brief is a narrative and narratives do not fail loudly. The PR-FAQ closes with a what-has-to-be-true list precisely because the rest reads as settled fact -- that list is an input to analysis, not the analysis. Something has to decide which claims would sink the idea if false, which anyone has evidence for, and what the cheapest way to find out is. Skipping it is how a plan gets built on the one claim nobody checked.

The template is Teresa Torres's Opportunity Solution Tree followed by David Bland's Assumption Mapping over its contents. They compose: the tree fixes what may be written down and where it attaches, the mapping fixes what gets tested first. A solution wired straight to the outcome is the visible symptom of a team that started from what it wanted to build, and the tree exists to make that visible on the page.

Two things are new work. Both formats are *drawings* in their sources and this beat must emit markdown a later beat can read, so the representation is fixed below. And discovery is where market sizing finally gets produced, one beat downstream of where the brief marked it unknown -- which creates a backward pull this issue closes: discovery must not fix up `brief.md`.

## Blocked by

Issue 01 (#15). `discovery.md` is the first member to carry a provenance line. Issue 02 (#16) is the upstream and a *soft* blocker.

## Deliverables

- **`SKILL.md`** -- input `product-brief`, successor `product-requirements`; states what happens when `brief.md` is absent.
- **`references/opportunity-solution-tree-template.md`**:
  1. **The tree**, four node layers with the connection rules stated as rules rather than implied by indentation: one Outcome at the root; an Opportunity space of customer needs discovered from evidence rather than invented; a Solution space whose every member attaches to exactly one opportunity; Assumption tests hanging off solutions. Every opportunity carries a required evidence field naming what it came from -- an interview, a ticket, an analytics figure -- or the unknown marker. Never omitted, never empty, because a blank field and an author's guess would otherwise look identical.
  2. **Assumption Mapping** -- every assumption scored on desirability, feasibility and viability and placed on the importance-versus-evidence two-by-two. One row each, fixed fields: statement, category, importance, evidence, quadrant, and the test that would settle it.
  3. **Riskiest assumption tests** -- an ordered list drawn from the high-importance, weak-evidence quadrant, cheapest first. Derived from the mapping, not chosen freely.
  4. **JTBD switch-interview structure** -- how the opportunity space gets populated with something other than the author's guesses.
  5. **Market sizing** -- TAM, SAM and SOM as nested figures, each with its method and source.

  **On-disk form:** every node carries a stable id and every non-root node names its parent by id, so the connection rules become mechanically checkable -- a solution whose parent is the outcome is a violation a reader can see without interpreting prose. A rendered diagram may accompany it; the id-bearing text is normative.
- **`references/product-discovery-principles.md`** -- four clusters: **unfalsifiable assumption** (no stated observation could show it false); **compound assumption** (two variables in one statement, so a failed test does not say which half failed); **solution attached straight to the outcome**; **experiment chosen for interest rather than risk**.
- **`tests/test_product_discovery_contract.py`.**

## Constraints

- **Never invent a fact.** This bites hardest on sizing, the one place this beat produces numbers: every figure carries its method and source, or the unknown marker.
- **Opportunities are marked by where they came from.** One resting on nothing but the author's reasoning is labelled as such rather than sitting indistinguishable beside one drawn from an interview.
- **Refuse a missing or non-conforming `brief.md`**, naming `product-brief`. Never infer an outcome from the slug: a tree with an invented root is the failure this beat exists to prevent.
- **Re-verify the JTBD stage names and the TAM/SAM/SOM definitions against a primary source** before freezing. Research asserts both but fetched no source for either, unlike the tree and the mapping. Freezing unverified stage names is how a plausible error becomes a contract.
- Inherits the epic's constraints. Constraint 10 bites here specifically: back-filling `brief.md` with the sizing it marked unknown would mark the `discovery.md` just written stale against it.

## Out of scope

Every other beat; the substrate. Conducting the research -- this produces the interview structure and the ordered list of tests worth running, not interviews, recruitment, experiments or evidence. Emitting requirements or acceptance criteria. Prioritizing work: the importance-versus-evidence quadrant ranks *assumptions by testing urgency*, which is not a delivery priority and must not be presented as one. Promoting JTBD or either canvas to an alternate template. Any change to `docs/plans/`, `/deep-plan`, or the existing four skills.

## References

- The four decisions this inherits, and the twelve cross-cutting constraints: the epic, #14.
- Imitate: `skills/design-review/SKILL.md` + `references/design-principles.md`, `skills/tdd-review/tests/`.
- Upstream, and owner of the unknown-marker token: issue 02 (#16).
- Opportunity Solution Tree: https://www.producttalk.org/opportunity-solution-trees/
- Assumption Mapping: https://www.strategyzer.com/library/testing-business-ideas
- JTBD and TAM/SAM/SOM: no primary source was fetched, which is why re-verification is a constraint above rather than a citation here.

title: 04. product-requirements skill -- convert validated opportunities into EARS requirements

labels.name: pre-planning
labels.description: Product lifecycle work upstream of /deep-plan

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

Third beat. Reads `discovery.md`, writes `requirements.md`: the opportunities discovery validated, stated in language a test can be written against.

Everything upstream is deliberately prose. A brief is a narrative and a discovery document is a set of ranked bets; neither is falsifiable at the level of a single sentence. "Users need a faster way to find their alerts" is a good opportunity and a useless acceptance condition, because two readers will build two different things and both believe they complied. This is where that ambiguity gets spent. It is separate from the spec because the failure modes differ: a spec fails by naming a library, a requirement fails by admitting more than one reading.

The template is EARS. It earns the slot because conformance is visible at the start of the sentence -- five patterns share one clause grammar and each licenses a keyword prefix, so a downstream beat can tell a requirement from a wish. Corroborated rather than invented: AWS Kiro ships `requirements.md` as one of three per-feature files and uses EARS for its acceptance criteria, so both filename and notation match a shipped convention.

Two things are new. EARS covers behaviour and says nothing about how much, how fast or how safely, so the template carries an ISO/IEC 25010 non-functional checklist and an INVEST gate for story-shaped requirements. And unusually for this suite, source material could not be read: the EARS paper is a binary PDF that would not extract, and the ISO page rendered only one of two pages. What follows is reconstruction, and re-verification is a constraint rather than a quiet assertion.

## Blocked by

Issue 01 (#15). Issue 03 (#17) is the upstream and a *soft* blocker -- build against the input contract plus its id-bearing opportunity nodes.

## Deliverables

- **`SKILL.md`** -- input `product-discovery`, successor `product-spec`; states what happens when `discovery.md` is absent.
- **`references/ears-template.md`**:
  1. **The five patterns**, each with its own clause grammar rather than summarised as a family: ubiquitous, event-driven (WHEN), state-driven (WHILE), unwanted behaviour (IF/THEN), optional feature (WHERE). Each carries a worked example, because the distinction authors get wrong most often -- an event that is really a state, a state that is really an optional feature -- is not conveyed by the grammar alone.
  2. **The combined general form**, showing how the optional clauses compose. This is what stops the five reading as five unrelated templates, so it is required rather than an appendix.
  3. **Identity and traceability** -- every requirement carries a stable id and names the discovery opportunity id it derives from. One tracing to no opportunity is the visible symptom of scope that entered without passing discovery.
  4. **The INVEST gate** for story-shaped requirements. EARS says nothing about size or independence, so a requirement can be perfectly well-formed and still be unbuildable as one unit. **This is the suite's single INVEST definition; issue 07 (#21) cites it.** Say so in the file.
  5. **The ISO/IEC 25010 non-functional checklist** -- the current revision's characteristics as prompts, each with a threshold and its source, or the unknown marker. A checklist rather than a section per characteristic: most products have nothing to say about most of them, and forcing a paragraph each produces filler that hides the two that matter.
- **`references/product-requirements-principles.md`** -- five clusters: **ambiguity**; **compound requirement** (two rules behind an "and", so a failing test does not say which half failed); **unverifiable**; **vague qualifier** ("user-friendly", "scalable", with no threshold); **imperative or UI-coupled Gherkin** ("When I click the login button" where "When I log in" belongs).
- **`tests/test_product_requirements_contract.py`.**

Gherkin appears in cluster 5 as an anti-pattern source and nowhere else -- the beat emits EARS. The cluster exists because Given/When/Then is what an author reaches for by reflex.

Clusters 1, 3 and 4 are close cousins of the Naming and Comments clusters in `skills/design-review/references/design-principles.md`. **Cite that file rather than re-deriving from it**; it declares itself the plugin's single source of truth for design guidance.

**The deliverable list is closed at four.** EARS is the most mechanically checkable template here, which makes a validator tempting. `scripts/` under a product skill is a shape only issue 01 (#15) has established; open a follow-up rather than forking that decision.

## Constraints

- **Never invent a threshold.** A latency, concurrency or availability figure carries its source or the unknown marker.
- **Every requirement traces to an opportunity**; one that does not is surfaced rather than written silently. Without this the beat degrades into a requirements list that happens to sit downstream of a discovery document.
- **Refuse a missing or non-conforming `discovery.md`**, naming `product-discovery`. Requirements invented without validated opportunities are what the chain exists to prevent, and this is where faking it is cheapest.
- **Re-verify the EARS keyword casing against the primary source.** Research could not extract the paper, so the casing of WHEN, WHILE, IF/THEN, WHERE and of `shall` versus `SHALL` is unconfirmed. If it stays unreachable, say so in the PR with what secondary sources agreed. Nothing downstream can tell a verified keyword from an invented one once it is in the template.
- **Re-verify the ISO/IEC 25010 list**, names and length both. Research reached Functional Suitability, Performance Efficiency, Compatibility, Interaction Capability, Reliability, Security, Maintainability and Portability, and reported at least one more did not render -- so the count itself is unconfirmed. Confirm the 2023 list and record the 2011 diff, of which the known part is Interaction Capability sitting where Usability used to. A checklist with a hole is worse than none, because a hole reads as completeness.
- Inherits the epic's constraints. This beat is more likely than its neighbours to be re-run in place, because requirements accrete as questions get answered; weigh that under constraint 12.

## Out of scope

Every other beat; the substrate. Deciding how anything is built -- no architecture, library, datastore, schema or interface design; mechanism is `/deep-plan` Phase 2's call, and a requirement naming a technology has smuggled a decision past two beats that exist to hold it. Authoring `spec.md`. Prioritizing, estimating or sequencing -- an ordered requirements list is a roadmap in disguise. Slicing into stories or issues, and any GitHub API call: INVEST judges whether a story-shaped requirement is well-formed, it does not cut anything up. Reviewing (issue 08 (#22)). A validator script or any `scripts/` directory. Promoting Gherkin or use cases to alternate templates.

## References

- The four decisions this inherits, and the twelve cross-cutting constraints: the epic, #14.
- Imitate, and the file clusters 1/3/4 cite: `skills/design-review/SKILL.md`, `references/design-principles.md`, `skills/tdd-review/tests/`.
- Upstream: issue 03 (#17). Second consumer of INVEST: issue 07 (#21).
- EARS paper, the casing source (binary PDF, could not extract): https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/5328509/
- EARS patterns, what the template was reconstructed from: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easy_Approach_to_Requirements_Syntax
- Kiro, precedent for filename and notation: https://kiro.dev/docs/specs/feature-specs/requirements-first/
- INVEST: https://xp123.com/articles/invest-in-good-stories-and-smart-tasks/
- ISO/IEC 25010, the list to re-verify: https://iso25000.com/index.php/en/iso-25000-standards/iso-25010
- Gherkin, source for cluster 5: https://cucumber.io/docs/gherkin/

title: 05. product-spec skill -- produce the spec.md that /deep-plan consumes

labels.name: pre-planning
labels.description: Product lifecycle work upstream of /deep-plan

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

Fourth beat. Reads `requirements.md`, writes `spec.md` -- the one member of the family that crosses into `/deep-plan`. Everything upstream exists to make it correct and nothing downstream reads any of them, because a planner that had to read four documents would re-derive the chain every run, and any one going stale would poison the plan silently.

Two properties follow, and they are the whole issue.

**No technology.** Mechanism is `/deep-plan` Phase 2's call, recorded in the plan's `## Decisions made` table. A spec that names a library or a datastore creates a second decision record, made earlier with less research, that nothing reconciles. No freshness check catches it: both documents are perfectly fresh and simply disagree.

**Self-contained.** The spec carries the problem, the validated opportunity, the in-scope requirements with their ids and acceptance conditions, and the non-goals, so the planner never opens `brief.md`, `discovery.md` or `requirements.md`. Links back are attribution, never a required click. This duplicates content that will drift, which is what the provenance line is for -- a stale roadmap misleads a reader, a stale spec feeds a plan.

## Blocked by

Issue 01 (#15), hard. Issue 04 (#18), soft. **Issue 10 (#24) is blocked by this one**, not the reverse: `spec.md` must be useful to a `/deep-plan` that was never taught its format -- plain prose markdown, no front-matter, no machine-readable block, nothing only the bridge would know how to read.

## Deliverables

- **`SKILL.md`** -- input `product-requirements`, successor `product-roadmap`, and `/deep-plan` as the consumer of the artifact. That third relationship is unique to this beat.
- **`references/spec-template.md`** -- modelled on spec-kit's `spec.md`; re-verify its section list against the source before freezing. Four things survive any divergence:
  1. The what and the why, no mechanism, with the reason stated where the author is writing.
  2. Carried-forward context: the problem and the validated opportunity restated, not cited.
  3. In-scope requirements, each with its id from `requirements.md` and its acceptance condition. A paraphrase with the condition dropped is the likeliest way this beat degrades, because paraphrasing reads like editing.
  4. Non-goals, required rather than optional.
- **`references/product-spec-principles.md`** -- five clusters: names a library or datastore; only makes sense to someone who read the brief; a requirement restated without its acceptance condition; no stated non-goals; and **non-goals with no cost** -- everything excluded is something nobody wanted anyway, so scope was described rather than decided. A choice whose rejected options all had obvious downsides was never a choice.
- **`tests/test_product_spec_contract.py`.**

## Constraints

- **Refuse a missing or non-conforming `requirements.md`**, naming `product-requirements`. Never write a spec from a brief, a discovery document, or the slug.
- **Every carried requirement traces to an upstream id**; one that does not is surfaced rather than written silently.
- **`spec-template.md` ships no front-matter and no machine-readable schema**, since a template that has one guarantees every spec written from it has one.
- **Take nothing else from spec-kit**: no constitution file, no numbered feature-branch folders, no `/speckit.*` command chain. Template adoption is where an unrelated workflow enters a repository by attachment.
- **A `spec.md` may already have been consumed by a plan**, so weigh that when choosing re-run behaviour under the epic's constraint 12.
- Inherits the epic's constraints.

## Out of scope

Every other beat; the substrate. Deciding how anything is built -- no architecture, library, datastore, schema, API shape, data model or file layout. That is the headline exclusion here, not boilerplate. Architecture decision records: the decision record for this chain is the plan's `## Decisions made` table, and an ADR here is the no-technology rule broken with better formatting. The bridge (issue 10 (#24)) -- no file under `skills/deep-plan/`. Prioritizing (06 / #20), slicing and filing (07 / #21), reviewing (08 / #22). A validator, a linter, or a banned-technology word list.

## References

- The four decisions this inherits, and the twelve cross-cutting constraints: the epic, #14.
- Imitate: `skills/design-review/SKILL.md` + `references/design-principles.md`, `skills/tdd-review/tests/`.
- The table this spec must not compete with: `skills/deep-plan/references/plan-file-template.md`.
- spec-kit -- filename, hand-off position, the what-and-why constraint, and the schema to re-verify: https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/spec-driven.md
- BMAD-METHOD, precedent for a self-contained handoff artifact: https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md
- Shape Up, precedent for No-gos as required: https://basecamp.com/shapeup/1.5-chapter-06
- Cluster 5: Gregor Hohpe, *The Software Architect Elevator*, ch. 8 -- attribute in the shipped file as `design-principles.md` does.

title: 06. product-roadmap skill -- order specified work into a sequence someone can bet on

labels.name: pre-planning
labels.description: Product lifecycle work upstream of /deep-plan

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

Fifth beat. Reads `spec.md`, writes `roadmap.md`: an ordered set of bets, each with a score explaining its position and a time budget it has to fit inside.

Not a dated timeline -- no quarters, no swimlanes, no features pinned to months. A date on unstarted work is a number nobody has a basis for. The naming has to survive a user who asked for a roadmap meaning the other thing.

Prioritization is the one beat where the framework is genuinely contested: RICE, ICE, WSJF, MoSCoW, Kano and Shape Up's betting table answer different questions, and two of them are not scoring formulas. The one-framework rule still applies, so RICE is the template and the rest are principles-file guidance -- but the skill must say both things, that RICE is fixed here *and* that prioritization has no canonical framework.

`roadmap.md` matches no shipped convention, unlike `requirements.md` and `spec.md`, so its section schema is authored here rather than inherited.

## Blocked by

Issue 01 (#15), hard -- and this beat authors `roadmap.md`'s H2 names, so it may update that one entry in `artifact-family.md` and nothing else. Issue 05 (#19), soft.

## Deliverables

- **`SKILL.md`** -- input `product-spec`, successor `product-issues`.
- **`references/rice-template.md`** -- the RICE table plus a Shape Up **appetite** column. Effort estimates size and divides the score; appetite is a fixed budget and is *not* an input to it. When effort exceeds appetite, reshape scope or drop the item, never raise the appetite. The two are in different units by default (person-time vs team calendar time), so the template states both and the conversion. Every number carries a basis field or the unknown marker. Plus the section schema, and the ordered sequence -- which is not the sorted score.
- **`references/product-roadmap-principles.md`** -- five clusters: false precision from multiplying guesses; padded confidence; **a score that ratifies a ranking already made**; **an ordering with no rejected alternative**; impact compared across teams as one currency. Plus guidance on when WSJF, MoSCoW, Kano, ICE or a betting table fit instead, including that RICE has no term for cost of delay.
- **`tests/test_product_roadmap_contract.py`.**

## Constraints

- No dates, quarters or sprints anywhere.
- Never invent an input; an item with an unknown input gets no score.
- The ordering is not the sorted score. Dependencies, appetite windows and human judgement outrank it, and the template gives that somewhere to be stated.
- Every row traces to `spec.md`. Refuse a missing one, naming `product-spec`.
- Re-verify reach and effort units against the original RICE post before freezing; research only reached secondary summaries, and effort is what appetite gets reconciled against. Check WSJF/MoSCoW/Kano/ICE against first-party sources or drop them.
- Re-scoring is routine and legitimate, so do not make re-runs awkward or destroy the previous scores.
- Inherits the epic's constraints.

## Out of scope

Other beats; the substrate beyond that one H2 entry; a second scoring instrument as template or flag; Shape Up's process (cycles, cool-down, pitches, shaping); Gantt, capacity or velocity modelling; story points and t-shirt sizes; slicing and filing (07 / #21); reviewing (08 / #22); a `scripts/` directory, including a score calculator -- a calculator makes the score look more authoritative than its inputs justify, which is the first cluster's whole point.

## References

- The four decisions this inherits, and the twelve cross-cutting constraints: the epic, #14.
- Imitate: `skills/design-review/SKILL.md` + `references/design-principles.md`, `skills/tdd-review/tests/`.
- RICE, units to re-verify: https://www.intercom.com/blog/rice-simple-prioritization-for-product-managers/
- Shape Up appetite: https://basecamp.com/shapeup/1.5-chapter-06 · WSJF: https://scaledagileframework.com/wsjf/
- MoSCoW, Kano and the ICE attribution have no fetched source and carry the same verification duty as the reach units.
- Clusters 3 and 4: Gregor Hohpe, *The Software Architect Elevator*, ch. 6 and 8 -- attribute in the shipped file as `design-principles.md` does.

title: 07. product-issues skill -- turn a prioritized roadmap into filed GitHub issues

labels.name: pre-planning

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

Last beat. Reads `roadmap.md`, cuts its top items into slices small enough for one implementer, and files them as GitHub issues under a tracking epic. **The only beat whose output leaves the repository**, and most of the spec follows from that.

Every other beat writes one markdown file: reviewable as a diff, revertible with `git checkout`, harmless to run twice. This one calls `gh` against a live repository, and a half-completed run leaves an unknown subset filed and no record of which. So it is two separable halves -- decide the slices and write them down, then file what was written -- with the filing half idempotent, guarded, and refusing rather than guessing when the environment is not what it expects.

The methodology is settled. SPIDR supplies the vocabulary for splitting an item along a dimension that keeps end-to-end user value; story mapping supplies the structure -- a backbone of the big steps a user takes, a walking skeleton forming the thinnest end-to-end release, later rows forming subsequent releases. Every release row crosses the whole backbone with user-visible value rather than implementing one layer. INVEST gates the result.

There is a second reason this must be built rather than left to a model's general knowledge of GitHub. Two facts contradict the documentation and both fail obscurely rather than loudly:

- **`gh issue create` has none of the `--parent`, `--blocked-by` or `--blocking` flags the manual documents.** Verified against 2.82.0 (2025-10-15), so this is not an old-version problem that waiting fixes.
- **The sub-issue REST endpoint wants GitHub's internal database id, not the issue number in the URL.** On this repository issue #25's database id is 5046900288 -- nine orders of magnitude apart, so a helper that posts the number links the wrong thing or nothing.

The working sequence, verified on this repository:

```
gh issue create --title ... --body-file ...     # prints the URL; the number is its trailing segment
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n} -q .id   # the child's database id
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{epic}/sub_issues -X POST -F sub_issue_id={id}
```

## Blocked by

Issue 01 (#15). Issue 04 (#18), for one thing: it ships the single INVEST definition and this skill cites it, and a citation cannot be asserted before its target exists. Issue 06 (#20) is the upstream and a *soft* blocker.

## Deliverables

- **`SKILL.md`** -- input `product-roadmap`; no successor, the chain ends here and `/deep-plan` picks up one filed issue at a time. Three rules fixed in the body:
  - **Two phases, as a rule.** Slice and write bodies to disk, show the user, then file. Writing to GitHub is behind an explicit flag and the default is a dry run. Every other beat can be undone with `git checkout`; this one cannot, and the default belongs on the side that can.
  - **Slices, not roadmap rows, are the unit filed.** One item may produce several issues. A skill that files one per row has skipped the beat and retyped the table.
  - What happens when `roadmap.md` is absent, and when the slug already has filed issues.
- **`references/story-map-template.md`** -- the backbone (derived from user activity, not system components); the walking skeleton as row one, with the test it must pass stated: *can someone use it, start to finish, badly?*; later release rows each crossing the backbone again; the five SPIDR patterns spelled out with examples, Spike carrying the caveat that it delivers no user value and is the last resort; **the INVEST gate by citation** of `skills/product-requirements/references/ears-template.md`, not by copy; per-slice fields (roadmap item id, backbone steps crossed, release row, acceptance condition, slices it must follow); and the emitted issue body's six H2 sections -- `## Context`, `## Blocked by`, `## Deliverables`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Out of scope`, `## References`. `## Blocked by` earns its place mechanically: the installed `gh` cannot express a blocked-by link, so ordering exists in the body text or nowhere.

  Output goes to `docs/product/<slug>/issues/`, a subfolder rather than a sixth member -- not indexed, not walked by `--check-freshness`. **Each emitted body carries the roadmap blob sha it was cut from** in its `## References`, because a filed issue is the one artifact living where no checker can reach it.
- **`scripts/file_issues.py`**, stdlib only. Six behaviours:
  1. **Capability guard on `gh`, detected not inferred** -- read the flags the local `gh` advertises rather than comparing versions, since the flags are absent at 2.82.0 and nobody knows which release will introduce them. Name the detected version and state which linking path was taken. REST is the path today; if a future `gh` grows `--parent`, taking it is an improvement, and either way an absent capability produces a named message rather than an obscure failure.
  2. **Idempotency check before creating.** `gh issue list --search` per title. The search is full-text and relevance-ranked, so a returned row is a candidate until its title is compared exactly client-side, and the index is not synchronous, so a just-created issue may not come back. Search guards a *later* run; the record file written as it goes guards the current one.
  3. **Labels and milestones created first.** `--label` and `--milestone` attach existing things and silently have nothing to attach otherwise. Labels via `gh label create`, checked against `gh label list`. There is no `gh milestone` command, so a milestone goes through `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/milestones`.
  4. **The documented ceilings respected**: 100 sub-issues per parent, 8 levels of nesting. Read the epic's count and position before linking and refuse, naming the ceiling. A batch wanting more than 100 children is a decomposition that went wrong several steps earlier.
  5. **Refuse to file any body still carrying the unknown marker.** Elsewhere that token is a sentence a reviewer catches in a diff; here it would be published and picked up by an implementer. Stop, name the file and the slice, file nothing at all -- a partial batch that omits the slice with the missing acceptance condition is the worst outcome, because it looks complete. State how the helper obtains that literal rather than leaving it to convenience.
  6. **Dry run by default**, printing the full intended sequence and touching nothing.
- **`references/product-issues-principles.md`** -- four clusters: **the horizontal or layer slice** ("build the database layer", "build the API") -- the flagship, because nothing is demoable until every layer for every feature is finished, and it is what a model produces by default since architectural layers are the most legible thing in any codebase; **the walking skeleton that swallowed the release**, where every slice ends up in row one and the first demoable increment moves to the end of the project; **slices with no upstream basis**; **the issue body that cannot be picked up alone**. Plus guidance on elephant carpaccio and the story-splitting flowcharts, which are not shipped as templates.
- **`tests/test_product_issues_contract.py`.** Real behaviour gets real tests. **Every `gh` invocation goes through one seam the tests substitute**, so the suite runs offline. That seam is not a test-only hook -- the dry run has to describe the same invocations without performing them, so it earns its place in the production path first.

## Constraints

- **No test makes a network call or creates an issue.** `uv run pytest` passes with no credentials and no network.
- **Fixtures are captured from real invocations**, not written from memory. Capture at least four before writing the tests: the `gh issue create --help` flag list, `gh label list`, an empty `sub_issues` array, and the `{id, node_id, number}` triple from `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}`. A hand-invented fixture turns every test green against a helper that cannot work.
- **Test the two overturned facts**, since both fail silently: the issue number read from the printed URL's trailing segment, and the `sub_issues` call sending the database id -- driven by a recorded response where the two differ by nine orders of magnitude, as they do here.
- **Verify the `--search` qualifier against a live repository** before relying on it. Research could not confirm it, and a check built on a qualifier that silently returns nothing reports "not filed yet" every time and duplicates the whole batch on the second run. Record what was run and what came back, and check for a secondary rate limit while you are there.
- **Every slice traces to a roadmap item id and a backbone step**; one with no upstream basis is surfaced, not filed.
- **Refuse a missing or non-conforming `roadmap.md`**, naming `product-roadmap`. Issues cut from an unprioritized source are a backlog, and the skipped beat is the one that decides what not to build.
- **Filed issues live outside the repository** and may have been edited, assigned or closed by people since. Anything treating them as regenerable output is wrong.
- **Confirm before building** that issue 01 (#15)'s test pins the five member *names* rather than banning other paths in the folder. If it bans them, raise it with issue 01 (#15) rather than editing that test.
- **Check the story-mapping vocabulary against primary sources**, the "walking skeleton" attribution specifically -- the term is Cockburn's and research reached it through Patton. Confirm the SPIDR expansions and Cohn's preference order too. Getting another author's vocabulary wrong in a file whose job is to teach it is worse than getting this suite's own conventions wrong.
- Inherits the epic's constraints.

## Out of scope

Every other beat; the substrate -- extending `--check-freshness` to walk `issues/` is issue 01 (#15)'s to take. Defining the unknown marker (02's / #16's) or INVEST (04's / #18's). The GraphQL `addSubIssue` mutation: research could not retrieve its field names from the live schema, and writing a mutation from memory is how a silent failure ships. Re-ordering or re-scoring roadmap items -- the input arrives ordered. Estimating: INVEST's Estimable asks whether a slice *could* be estimated, not for a number. Dates, sprints, milestone-as-schedule. Projects boards, field automation, issue types, assignees, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`. Editing, closing or reordering existing issues, and the unlink endpoints -- undoing a batch is a human operation. Filing to any repository other than the resolved one. Reviewing (08 / #22). Re-filing or reconciling the eleven issues of this batch, which were filed by hand.

## References

- The four decisions this inherits, and the twelve cross-cutting constraints: the epic, #14.
- Imitate: `skills/design-review/SKILL.md` + `references/design-principles.md`, `skills/deep-plan/scripts/`, `skills/tdd-review/tests/`.
- Owner of the INVEST definition this cites: issue 04 (#18). Upstream: issue 06 (#20).
- SPIDR: https://www.mountaingoatsoftware.com/blog/spidr
- Story mapping: https://jpattonassociates.com/the-new-backlog/ (see the attribution caveat above)
- INVEST: https://xp123.com/articles/invest-in-good-stories-and-smart-tasks/
- `gh issue create` flags and the URL it prints: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_issue_create
- Sub-issue REST endpoints and the `sub_issue_id` requirement: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/sub-issues
- The 100-sub-issue and 8-level ceilings: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/adding-sub-issues
- `gh label create`/`list`, and the absence of `gh milestone`: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_label_create
- Milestones over REST: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/milestones

body:
## Context

The plugin's plan artifacts are trustworthy because nothing in them is taken on the author's word: a critic fleet reads each against a file of red-flag clusters and an adversarial verify pass tries to refute every finding. The new suite ships six principles files. Without this issue it ships six rubrics and nothing that reads them, and product artifacts become the only ones in the repository nobody argues with.

This is cheap, and why is the whole argument for shipping principles files alongside templates. **`deep-plan:dp-critic` carries no rubric of its own** -- its entire question set arrives in the caller's prompt, quoted from a cluster source the caller names. Phase 4.6 already runs that one leaf four times against four different sources. A product principles file is simply a fifth, sixth and seventh. So this costs one thin skill, no new agent, and no disturbance to the pin that exactly one agent may write.

The deliverable should stay small. `design-review/SKILL.md` and `tdd-review/SKILL.md` are each about fifty lines: resolve a target, run the recipe, report. This is the third of that shape, differing in one respect, which is what it owns: **its cluster source is not fixed.** It arms a different rubric depending on which member it was pointed at, so resolving the target and selecting the rubric are one step.

That rests on the epic's constraint 2. The triage gate consumes cluster names from the H3 headings and each finder consumes one cluster's questions verbatim, so a rubric in any other shape is a file this skill cannot run. This is the issue that breaks when a sibling ignores it.

## Blocked by

- **Issue 01 (#15).** The mapping from member to rubric is only total because the member set is closed. Without that pin the rule has an undefined branch for every filename someone drops in the folder.
- **Any one authoring issue among 02 (#16) through 06 (#20).** Issue 02 (#16) is the natural first.

Deliberately *not* blocked on all six -- that would schedule the consumer of the cluster shape after every producer of it, which is the ordering most likely to produce five rubrics each needing a follow-up edit. The test is written over the files that *exist*, so coverage grows on its own.

## Deliverables

- **`SKILL.md`** (`argument-hint: "[product-member | slug]"`). Six things fixed:
  - Reads `skills/design-review/references/fleet-orchestration.md` and the selected principles file at run time, restating neither.
  - **Target resolution.** A member path reviews that member; a bare slug reviews every member present, one fleet run each; an empty argument asks via `AskUserQuestion` rather than guessing.
  - **Rubric selection as one literal path template**, not a table of cases: member `<member>.md` selects `skills/product-<member>/references/product-<member>-principles.md`. It appears verbatim in that placeholder form, because the test lifts it and substitutes the member set rather than keeping a second copy of the rule.
  - **Agent type is `deep-plan:dp-critic` and nothing else.** Targets are passed as text excerpts or file paths; the critics have no Bash.
  - **A missing or malformed rubric is reported, not degraded.** Say which file and which member and stop. Never fall back to another member's rubric and never invent clusters -- a run against the wrong rubric reads as a clean review.
  - **Report only.** Findings grouped material-then-minor, a one-line verdict, no edits. Fixes offered only if the user asks, as in `design-review` Step 3.
- **`tests/test_product_review_contract.py`.**
- **One line added to the pairing list** in `fleet-orchestration.md`, registering `skills/product-*/references/product-*-principles.md` as a cluster source for `dp-critic`, and updating the count in the same sentence. The only file outside `skills/product-review/` and `pyproject.toml` this issue may touch: the recipe is the single home for which leaf pairs with which rubric, and a pairing that exists in practice but not in that list is the gap that persuades the next caller to add an agent type.

**What this must not add, stated as a deliverable because it is the point: no new agent.** A product critic would be a byte-for-byte copy of a rubric-free leaf differing only in a description, and every file under `agents/` lands inside a test whose writable-agent set is an explicit constant precisely so adding one is a deliberate edit.

## Constraints

- **The mapping is tested by derivation, not against a hard-coded list.** A test cannot evaluate prose: it would regex-match the sentence (proving the sentence exists) or reimplement the rule (testing its own copy). So the test lifts the template, substitutes each member name, and asserts every `product-*-principles.md` in the tree is produced by exactly one member and no substitution escapes `skills/product-*/references/`.
- **Assert the cluster shape for every rubric the mapping reaches.** Each authoring issue asserts it locally; the duplication is deliberate, because a local test passes in a repository where the constraint is honoured six slightly different ways and only the consumer sees them together.
- **Do not restate fleet mechanics** -- no step list, no session cap, no loop bound, no severity vocabulary. Assert the pointer instead.
- **Do not re-pin the agent inventory or the writable-agent set.** `test_agents_contract.py` owns both.
- **State that this skill runs from the main thread**, so the recipe's `## Nested fleets` obligations do not apply. The two preceding review skills leave that implicit and it is the most misread part of the recipe. Workflow path preferred; absence, denial or error falls back without asking.
- **Never edit the artifact it reviews.** Five members carry a provenance line, and silently editing one changes the content a downstream sha was taken over -- review would manufacture the staleness it was never asked to judge.
- **A slug target produces one findings block per member**, never merged: one fleet run consumes one cluster source, so the member a finding came from is also the rubric it was judged against.
- **The pairing edit leaves `test_design_review_contract.py` passing** and must not renumber or reword the existing pairings.
- **Stay comparable in size to the two existing review skills.** Growth past them is rubric content, which belongs in a sibling's `references/`.
- Inherits the epic's constraints.

## Out of scope

Everything under `agents/`. Authoring any principles content -- no default rubric, no shared fallback, no clusters for a member whose issue has not landed. Reviewing `docs/plans/` artifacts; this must not become a second entry point to plan review. Staleness and chain state (09 / #23) -- a stale member is perfectly reviewable, so this reads no provenance line. Fixing anything. Gating: it never blocks a beat and is never invoked on the user's behalf, because a reviewer that gates is an orchestrator with a modest description. Any further change to the recipe beyond the pairing line. Wiring this into Phase 4.6 or any beat's body.

## References

- The four decisions this inherits, and the twelve cross-cutting constraints: the epic, #14.
- The recipe, the triage gate, and the pairing list this extends: `skills/design-review/references/fleet-orchestration.md`.
- The two wrappers to imitate: `skills/design-review/SKILL.md`, `skills/tdd-review/SKILL.md`.
- The leaf reused as-is: `agents/dp-critic.md`.
- One leaf against several cluster sources: `## Phase 4.6` of `skills/deep-plan/SKILL.md` and the Phase 4.6 fragment of `references/phase-prompts.md`.
- Pins not to disturb: `skills/deep-plan/tests/test_agents_contract.py`, `skills/design-review/tests/test_design_review_contract.py`.
- Existing cluster sources whose shape every product rubric must match: `readability-principles.md`, `plan-integrity-principles.md`.
- Sibling sharing the `product-<member>` derivation: issue 09 (#23).

title: 09. product-status skill -- report where a slug is in the chain and what is stale

labels.name: pre-planning
labels.description: Product lifecycle work upstream of /deep-plan

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

The suite is flat with no orchestrator. That buys what it was chosen for -- each beat is an issue someone can pick up alone -- and leaves one hole: an orchestrator knows where you are, and a flat suite does not. Nothing can answer the two questions a user asks between beats: *where am I*, and *what have I written that has since gone out of date*. This skill answers both, reading `docs/product/<slug>/` and reporting rather than acting.

The staleness half is not new work: the substrate already ships `--check-freshness`, which reports and never decides. This is the surface that carries that report to the user, and re-implements none of it.

The other half is discovery, and it is why this is not merely a convenience. In a flat suite a user who does not know it exists has nowhere to find out which beat is next. `obra/superpowers` ships fourteen flat skills and one thin meta-skill, `using-superpowers`, whose whole job is to force a discovery check -- it coordinates without controlling. This is the deliberate analogue, with one difference: `using-superpowers` is always-active and this is not, because an always-active skill taxes every turn including the overwhelming majority with nothing to do with product work. The consequence belongs in the pull request rather than being discovered later: **discovery here is pull, not push**, and a user who never invokes this gets no prompt to.

## Blocked by

**Issue 01 (#15).** Hard, and the strongest in the batch. This skill has no logic beyond a report format -- the folder, the slug, the closed member set that makes "which are missing" a total answer, the provenance line and `--check-freshness` all come from issue 01 (#15).

Deliberately **not** blocked on 02 through 08. "Four of five members missing" is a correct status report. The test ranges over the `skills/product-*/` directories that exist, so coverage grows on its own.

## Deliverables

- **`SKILL.md`** (`argument-hint: "[slug]"`). Six things fixed:
  - **It declares `allowed-tools`, and that is load-bearing.** Three rules -- never writes, never launches agents, never invokes another skill -- are prose in every sibling issue and so only checkable at review time. Declaring the tool set makes them a static assertion: `Write`, `Edit`, `Agent`, `Skill` all absent. Not bare `Bash` either, since a shell writes files and granting it hands back exactly what the other three exclusions removed; scope it to the one command, in the `Bash(<command>:*)` form the plugin's permission rules already use.
  - **It runs the substrate rather than re-deriving anything.** Staleness comes from `--check-freshness` and nowhere else. No restating the staleness rule, the provenance format or the member set, and no shelling out to `git hash-object` -- the shortcut that would put a second copy of the drift rule in the repository.
  - **It reads that output as text, not as a parsed structure.** A skill is a model reading command output, not a program consuming an API. One requirement does fall on issue 01 (#15) and should be raised there: `--check-freshness` must be addressable at a single slug.
  - **No slug reports every slug, one line each, and asks nothing.** Issue 08 (#22) pins the opposite for the same empty argument and the divergence is deliberate, so record the reason: a review is several fleet runs and asking beats guessing wrong, while a status report is a folder listing and a script call, so asking costs a turn to get an answer that was free. A single slug present reports in full, since a menu of one is a prompt with no choice in it.
  - **One line per member in chain order, then exactly one recommendation.** Never alphabetical: `roadmap.md` sorts before `spec.md`, which prints the last two beats backwards at exactly the point where "where am I" matters most.
  - **The recommendation is a total rule with a stated order**: first *missing* member wins; else first *stale* member, recommending a re-run of its owning beat; else `product-issues`. An `unresolvable` member is reported prominently and never changes the answer, because a malformed provenance line is fixed by an edit rather than a re-run. An empty or absent folder recommends `product-brief` -- the cold-start case, and the most valuable answer this skill gives.
  - **The member-to-skill derivation is cited, not restated.** Per the epic's paired rule, whichever of this and issue 08 (#22) lands second promotes it into `artifact-family.md`'s member table and converts the first's copy into a citation. **The only substrate edit this issue makes.**
- **`tests/test_product_status_contract.py`.**

**What this must not add, stated as a deliverable because it is the point: no `status.md`.** It would break the closed member set and create the one artifact with no upstream and no provenance line -- a cache of a computation that is cheap to redo and wrong the moment any member changes.

## Constraints

- **The recommendation rule is tested by derivation**, reading chain order and the owning-skill column from `artifact-family.md` rather than a second copy, and asserting every `skills/product-*/` beat present is named by exactly one member and no member names a skill outside it.
- **`SKILL.md` does not restate the member set, chain order, provenance format or staleness rule.** The obvious assertion is wrong: banning every member filename would fail on the cold-start rule, which legitimately names `product-brief`, and on any worked example. What is banned is the *enumeration* -- count how many member names appear literally and fail when all of them do. Naming one is an example; naming the set is a copy. The provenance literal is banned outright.
- **Frontmatter assertions are direct, not prose-matched**: `allowed-tools` declared; `Write`/`Edit`/`Agent`/`Skill` absent; no bare `Bash`; `disable-model-invocation` absent or false, since this is the one skill that must stay model-invocable; `user-invocable` not false.
- **Re-verify** whether `allowed-tools` honours the `Bash(<command>:*)` form or only bare tool names. If not, say so in the PR and keep the prose rule rather than silently widening the grant.
- **Staleness stays a finding.** No non-zero exit, no truncated report, no "blocked" language. A consumer that treats it as an error has re-introduced the gate the flat design rejected.
- **An unresolvable slug or absent `docs/product/` produces a report, not an error.** "Nothing written yet, start with `product-brief`" is the correct answer to "where am I".
- Inherits the epic's constraints.

## Out of scope

Writing anything into `docs/product/<slug>/` -- no `status.md`, no cache, no index row, no back-filling a missing member. Re-implementing freshness: if `--check-freshness` cannot answer something, the fix is an issue against the substrate. Deciding what to do about staleness. Reviewing content (08 / #22) -- this ships no principles file, no clusters, no fleet, no agent. **The plugin-wide description-budget test**, which globs over `skills/*/SKILL.md`, constrains files eight other issues own, and needs its own doc re-verification: that is issue 11 (#25), not a second job bolted onto a status reporter. Gating in every form. Editing any sibling skill. `docs/plans/` chain state.
