title: 10. spec.md bridge into /deep-plan Phase 1 -- detect a spec and offer it as a planning source

labels.name: pre-planning
labels.description: Product lifecycle work upstream of /deep-plan

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

Everything else in this batch builds new files. This is the only one that changes a skill that already ships, and it is the reason the other nine are worth building.

Of the five members, exactly one crosses into planning: `spec.md`. Issue 05 (#19) makes it self-contained on purpose, so a planner never opens the other three. Today nothing on the planning side knows the file can exist: a user who has just spent four beats writing the definitive statement of a body of work runs `/deep-plan <topic>` and is asked, from scratch, whether they happen to have any source material. The document is one directory over, named after the same initiative, written for this exact consumer.

**The fix is deliberately not an integration.** Phase 1 already launches `dp-source-ingest` when the user supplied sources, and already asks once via `AskUserQuestion` when it detected none. Both the mechanism and the moment exist; what is missing is that the skill never looks where the answer most likely is. So this adds a detection and changes what an existing question offers -- no new phase, agent, artifact, or obligation in either direction.

That restraint is the design. A bridge that parsed the spec, wired the product slug to the plan slug, or ingested without asking would convert a suggestion into a coupling and make each side's correctness depend on the other's, so the two families would have to be versioned together -- the cost the flat design was chosen to avoid. If this issue is reverted, both sides still work.

Two facts shape the whole deliverable and are easy to get wrong from the plan alone.

**The plan's slug does not exist yet in Phase 1.** `/deep-plan` builds it in Phase 4 from intent keywords plus the top two decision choices; until then the work lives in `<topic>-draft/`. So the match cannot mean "the folder named after this plan's slug" -- there is no such string yet, and when there is it derives from decisions this run has not taken. Match over the topic text, at Phase 1 time; the two slugs stay independent forever.

**Phase 1 caps itself at one instance of each agent type.** A detected spec joins the single `dp-source-ingest` launch or it is not ingested at all.

## Blocked by

- **Issue 01 (#15)**, specifically its `--exists` entry point. This is the family's first pure reader; the other three entry points are writer-shaped.
- **Issue 05 (#19).** The offer is only a good one once the member is specified to be self-contained. Bridging to a `spec.md` whose shape nobody fixed would seed plans from a document with no guaranteed content, and the failure would be invisible: the plan would look coherent and rest on half a specification.

Not blocked on 08 or 09. **Land this last of the ten** -- it is the only child editing shipped, contract-tested behaviour, and its value is zero until a user has written a spec.

## Deliverables

Three files inside `skills/deep-plan/` plus one README line. The shortness of the list is itself the deliverable.

- **`SKILL.md`, the Phase 1 section only.** The `dp-source-ingest` bullet gains the detection and the offer. Six behaviours:
  - **Exact match over the normalised topic**, via `--exists`.
  - **No fuzzy matching, ever.** If the normalised topic names no folder, be silent even when a plausibly related one sits next to it. A near-match seeds the plan from another initiative's specification and nothing downstream notices, because the result is internally consistent. The cost of strictness is nil -- the user can paste the path at the same question.
  - **Silent when there is nothing to offer.** No `docs/product/`, no match, or a match with no `spec.md`, and Phase 1 behaves exactly as today: same question, same options, no extra prompt, no extra subprocess beyond the single existence check. Most runs have no product folder and must not pay for this in latency or noise.
  - **Folder present, `spec.md` absent, is silence too.** No offering `requirements.md` instead. A bridge that widens itself under scarcity is how the "planner never reads four documents" property dies.
  - **The offer is a question, never an automatic ingest, and never a second question.** Where Phase 1 asks its source question today, the spec becomes the recommended first option. Where the user already supplied sources and Phase 1 asks nothing, it still has to be asked -- silently appending a file the user did not name is the automatic ingest this bans -- but as that same single question, so the blocking prompt count stays at most one either way.
  - **Freshness surfaced inside the offer, only after a hit.** Run `--check-freshness` and state staleness inside the question so the user chooses with the drift visible. Stale is not a veto. If the check cannot run, the offer proceeds without that line -- a failure to describe the file must never suppress the offer or fail Phase 1.
- **`references/phase-prompts.md`, the Phase 1 fragment only** -- the same behaviour in its own voice, including the revised option list. Both files state it because the test asserts over both regions, as `test_phase46_gates_the_fleet_on_triage` already does.
- **A new test function in `skills/deep-plan/tests/test_skill_contract.py`** -- not a new module. That file already resolves both regions, so no packaging change of any kind.
- **One README line beside the existing floor sentence.** Stacking skills in one message needs v2.1.199; the README states v2.1.142 for the Task dependency API. **Do not raise the floor** -- that number exists for a load-bearing runtime dependency, and inflating it for documentation convenience locks out working installations to buy a nicer usage example. Note instead that suite skills are invoked one per message and stacking additionally requires v2.1.199. Two sentences at most, and the only file outside `skills/deep-plan/` this issue may touch.

**What this must not add, stated as a deliverable because it is the point:** no new phase, agent, checkpoint, sentinel, or plan-folder member. The detection reuses the project root Phase 0 already resolved, and an ingested spec's provenance is already carried by `user_source_summary`. If the implementation finds itself adding a phase heading, the design has been misread.

## Constraints

Most of these are prohibitions, and a prohibition is satisfied by absence -- delete the bridge and every "fails if" still passes. So the test needs a positive anchor first.

- **Positive anchor**: both regions name `docs/product/`, `spec.md` and `dp-source-ingest` together.
- **`## Phase ` headings pinned as an explicit list**, so adding a phase is a visible edit to a test constant rather than a side effect.
- **Checkpoint 1 survives verbatim** in both files -- question string, `Header: "Scope"`, four options. Scope confirmation is where the user says what is being planned, and a detected spec must not answer that for them.
- **No agent type named beyond the three Phase 1 launches today**, and no file added to `agents/`.
- **The one-instance cap sentence is not weakened**, and both regions state the spec joins the single launch rather than adding one. Most likely to be violated by an implementation that reads "launch per source" from the agent's own description and stops there.
- **No `docs/product/` member named but `spec.md`**, asserted by absence of the other four.
- **Neither region stops naming `AskUserQuestion`**, or describes the ingest as automatic or unprompted.
- **The substrate script reached only through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.** A resolved path works until the next update and then silently stops detecting anything, which presents as the feature never having been built.
- **The test must not re-pin the member set, slug rules, or provenance format.** `skills/product-artifacts/tests/` owns all three; the only product-side string this test may know is `spec.md`.
- **Re-verify the version floor.** If the documented minimum has reached v2.1.199 by the time this lands, drop the README line rather than adding it -- a note about a floor everyone clears is noise that outlives its reason.
- **The existing suite passes unchanged**, with no edit to any other test file. If an existing assertion has to be relaxed, the change is wrong, because every one of them describes behaviour this issue promised not to touch.
- **An end-to-end check by hand, recorded in the PR**: run `/deep-plan <topic>` with no `docs/product/` and confirm Phase 1 is byte-identical to today, then with a matching `spec.md` and confirm the offer appears, declines cleanly, and leaves the run indistinguishable from the first.

## Out of scope

Any change to `/deep-plan` outside Phase 1 -- not Phase 0, not Phase 2's decisions, not Phase 4's slug construction or plan folder, not 4.6, 5, or execute. The plan slug and product slug stay independent in both directions. Any write anywhere: no `--ensure-folder`, no provenance authored, no marking a spec consumed, no back-link. Parsing `spec.md` -- no section extraction, no validation, no rejecting a malformed one; it is handed over as a path exactly as a user-supplied path is, and issue 05 (#19) wrote it for a consumer that was never taught its format. Every product skill and the substrate. Gating in either direction, including `product-spec` invoking `/deep-plan`, which would give the flat suite an orchestrator by accident at its last beat. Reporting on the family (09 / #23). Reviewing (08 / #22). Multi-slug or interactive selection -- exactly one exact match or nothing. Documenting the suite in the README.

## References

- The four decisions this inherits, and the twelve cross-cutting constraints: the epic, #14.
- Edit points: `## Phase 1: Parallel triangulation` of `skills/deep-plan/SKILL.md`, and the Phase 1 fragment of `references/phase-prompts.md`. Phase 1's cap, its source question and Checkpoint 1's options all live there.
- Why the plan slug is unavailable in Phase 1: `## Phase 4` of `SKILL.md`, and `scripts/resolve_slug.py`.
- The consumer reused unchanged: `agents/dp-source-ingest.md`.
- The test file to extend and the both-regions shape to imitate: `tests/test_skill_contract.py`, `test_phase46_gates_the_fleet_on_triage`.
- The floor sentence this annotates rather than raises: `README.md`, "Requires Claude Code >= v2.1.142".
- Skill stacking's version gate, to re-verify: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
- Blockers: issue 01 (#15) (and its `--exists` entry point), issue 05 (#19).

title: 11. skill description budget -- one globbed assertion for the whole plugin

labels.name: pre-planning
labels.description: Product lifecycle work upstream of /deep-plan

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

repository.name: claude-better-plan
repository.description: A Better plan skill with more questions to the user, research online and an easier way of creating plans.

body:
## Context

Skill auto-invocation is description-match driven, and descriptions compete for a shared listing budget of roughly one percent of the context window. On overflow, Claude Code drops descriptions starting from the least-recently-invoked skill. The pre-planning suite adds eight near-identically phrased `SKILL.md` files on top of the four that exist -- precisely the shape that degrades -- and the beats a user runs least lose their descriptions first.

The arithmetic, because it is what turns a documented risk into a deliverable. An earlier measurement put the four existing descriptions at 349, 390, 519 and 647 characters -- 1,905 total, comfortable -- but that record is gone, so re-measure before relying on it. Twelve at that mean is roughly 5,700. One percent of a 200,000-token window is about 2,000 tokens, call it 8,000 characters, and that is shared with every other installed plugin, every project skill and every personal skill the user has. This plugin alone would claim most of it. Nothing in the chain is a hard error; the failure is silent, asymmetric, and lands on the beats used least.

The enforcement problem is separate, and it is why this is an issue rather than a line in another one. `skills/deep-plan/tests/test_skill_contract.py` checks frontmatter against three hard-coded constants and does not cover `skills/tdd-review/SKILL.md` at all; that skill's own description pin ended up in `skills/tdd-review/tests/test_test_principles_contract.py`, a different directory under a different test's name. **A per-skill constant list did not survive four skills and will not survive twelve.** Enumerate by glob, once, for the whole plugin.

Originally folded into issue 09 (#23). Separated because it is plugin-wide, constrains files eight other issues own, needs its own doc re-verification, and has nothing to do with reporting where a slug is in the chain.

## Blocked by

Nothing mechanically -- the test can land against the four existing skills and strengthen as siblings arrive. Sequence it early anyway: the trigger-phrase rule is the epic's constraint 4, cheap from the first beat and expensive to retrofit across eight.

## Deliverables

- **A globbed test**, in a location no single skill owns:
  - `skills/*/SKILL.md` -- every skill, not only the new ones -- for the **aggregate ceiling**. A budget is shared by definition, so measuring only the eight new descriptions measures nothing. The ceiling is a literal number with its derivation in a comment beside it: window size, the one-percent figure, characters per token, the share this plugin may claim. A ceiling with no recorded arithmetic is a number the next contributor raises rather than a constraint.
  - `skills/product-*/SKILL.md` for the per-skill rules: under the per-skill cap, and a distinguishing trigger phrase in the **first sentence**. The `product-` prefix is part of that surface but a prefix alone does not distinguish `product-spec` from `product-requirements`; the first sentence must name the artifact or question the skill owns before it says anything the siblings also say.
- **A written `disable-model-invocation` evaluation** covering all twelve skills, carried into the epic. Starting position, to be confirmed or overturned below: `product-status`, `product-brief` and `product-review` stay model-invocable, because those are the cold-start surfaces -- a user says "where am I", "write me a product brief", or "review this brief" without knowing the suite exists. The five mid-and-late-chain beats are the candidates, because each is reached from a chain position `product-status` reports rather than cold. The mechanism is not novel: `skills/deep-plan/SKILL.md` already ships it.

## Constraints

- **Re-verify one load-bearing fact first**: does `disable-model-invocation: true` remove a description from the model-facing listing entirely, or only stop auto-invocation while the description still occupies budget? If the latter, the mitigation frees nothing, the evaluation is worthless, and the only lever left is shorter descriptions -- which changes the recommendation but not the aggregate assertion. Land the answer in the PR; do not ship on the assumption.
- **Reconcile the per-skill cap to one number in one place.** Two figures are in circulation: 1,536 characters for `description` plus `when_to_use`, and the under-1024 that `test_test_principles_contract.py` asserts. Only the second is in the repository and neither has a live citation, so re-verify against the docs. Pick one and leave exactly one assertion of it -- if the 1024 survives it moves, if the globbed one supersedes it the old one is deleted, not left beside it.
- **Both assertions fail loudly with the measured number**, since a budget test whose failure does not say by how much is one the next contributor guesses at.
- **`test_skill_contract.py` still passes unchanged.** This adds coverage; it does not take over that file's existing assertions.
- **This issue may edit a sibling's `description` frontmatter and nothing else** if one landed non-compliant first. The alternative is a test that is red on arrival for a reason its own deliverables cannot fix.
- Inherits the epic's constraints.

## Out of scope

Every skill's behaviour, body, references and tests -- this touches `description` lines and adds one test file. Adding `disable-model-invocation: true` to any beat: this issue writes the evaluation, each beat's issue makes the change. Rewriting the four existing descriptions, unless the aggregate cannot pass without it, in which case say so in the PR rather than editing quietly. The artifact family, the substrate, any template.

## References

- The baseline figures above (349 / 390 / 519 / 647) come from a prior measurement whose record was not committed. Re-measure the four shipped `SKILL.md` descriptions as the first step, and derive the ceiling from what you actually find rather than from those numbers.
- The budget, the per-skill cap, `disable-model-invocation`, the drop rule: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
- The contract this extends and the enumerate-by-constant pattern it replaces: `skills/deep-plan/tests/test_skill_contract.py`.
- The assertion to reconcile: `skills/tdd-review/tests/test_test_principles_contract.py`.
- In-repo precedent for `disable-model-invocation: true`: `skills/deep-plan/SKILL.md`.
- Where this came from: issue 09 (#23), which originally carried it.
